resourceName: Enteric fermentation emissions' reduction program of Uruguay
description:
“Enteric fermentation emissions‘ reduction program of Uruguay” is taken place in a country where livestock farming covers a total area of 12,9 million hectares which represents 70% of the total national area (DIEA, 2021). This sector accounts for 57% of national net emissions, of which more than half correspond to methane emissions from enteric fermentation of livestock. This project will comprise approximately 100,000 animals per year, starting with a feedlot of 1,500 animals. In this system animals enter a feedlot with a weight of 415 kg and finish after 110 days with 590 kg. The breeds involved in the feedlot systems are Angus, Hereford and their crossbreeds.
The project will result in a reduction of methane emissions from enteric fermentation in beef cattle and dairy cows by providing a natural additive of composed by essential oils, flavonoids, and tannins: Anavrin. Anavrin® is a product that has been tested in recent years at the universities of Milan, Sassari, Santa Maria in Brazil, and at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine of UdelaR in Uruguay. In addition, tests have been carried out in other parts of the world, where it was highlighted that the correct use of Anavrin® also improves the animal's daily production, around 70 g, and 1,5 l daily milk gain per capita. This a grouped project that starts with a farm located in the department of “Flores” near its capital city, The project start date is 1st April 2022. New instances (farmers) will be part of the project, benefiting from the use of the product itself but also from the generation of carbon credits, which will be seen as a reduction of the purchase price of the product. In 10 years, the project will be generating 100.000 tCO2, based on the preliminary estimations done by yet to be published papers. The project will monitor the emissions reductions according to VM0041 methodology by direct measurements.
